Evelyn Everett-Green wrote this tale of the Gunpowder Plot days, centered on the lost treasure of Trevlyn. Chapters move from the old gate house and Trevlyn Chase into London town. A wise woman, a hunted priest, and gypsies appear. A lone house on the river brings peril for Trevlyn. Yuletide at the Cross Way House closes the tale. Cuthbert, Cherry, Kate, and Jacob carry the plot.

Everett-Green blends history with family adventure, as young folk hunt treasure while priests hide and plots brew. The tale teaches loyalty, courage, and faith without preaching at length. Young readers get a brisk, old-style historical adventure, full of heaths, forests, and secret ways, set in a dangerous year for English Catholics.

Evelyn Everett-Green wrote The Lost Treasure of Trevlyn, a story of the days of the Gunpowder Plot. Her chapter list moves from the inmates of the old gate house and Trevlyn Chase to the lost treasure itself. Then it runs through a hunted priest, a wise woman, a gipsy's tryst and warning, and peril for Trevlyn. Chapter one opens mid-quarrel at the gate house, where an angry old man storms at a boy who will not simply submit. The father curses the boy as heretic spawn and denies he is any father to him.

Everett-Green starts with a household split by religion in the years of the Plot. Young readers get family conflict, hidden treasure, and Catholic peril under a Protestant state, all promised by the chapter titles and the opening scene.
